timeout.label: DB statement timeout (ms)
timeout.help: Per-query Postgres timeout. Prevents a runaway query from exhausting the pool. 0 = no timeout.

maxRows.label: Max result rows
maxRows.help: Hard ceiling on rows returned, regardless of the requested limit.

contextTurns.label: Context turns
contextTurns.help: Number of previous Q&A turns loaded as short-term memory for follow-up questions.

pbiResolve.label: Resolve filter values
pbiResolve.help: Check the values the assistant filters on against the real values in the model, correcting typos and asking when a name is ambiguous. Turning this off sends filter values through to DAX exactly as written.

pbiThreshold.label: Match threshold
pbiThreshold.help: How close a value must be to count as the same value, 0–100. Lower accepts more typos but asks for confirmation less often.

pbiDomain.label: Values read per column
pbiDomain.help: Ceiling on how many distinct values are read from a column when checking one. Higher is more accurate on large dimensions but slower.

pbiCross.label: Search related columns
pbiCross.help: When a value is not in the column the assistant picked, look for it in sibling columns of the same table (e.g. a model name given as a product name).

sqlResolve.label: Resolve filter values
sqlResolve.help: Check SQL filter values against authorized source values before query generation. It corrects one unambiguous typo and asks before choosing among alternatives.

sqlThreshold.label: Match threshold
sqlThreshold.help: How close a source value must be to count as a typo correction.

sqlDomain.label: Values read per column
sqlDomain.help: Maximum source values checked for one SQL filter. Higher improves coverage but can add latency.

sqlTimeout.label: Lookup deadline (ms)
sqlTimeout.help: Stop a single MCP or database value lookup after this time and leave the literal unverified.

sqlCache.label: Verified-value cache (seconds)
sqlCache.help: How long user-scoped, complete value domains may be reused.

metaEvidence.label: Use Schema Modeler profiles and captured values
metaEvidence.help: Read column profiles and captured distinct values (metadata DB or MCP profile tools) before touching the source. Corrects typos from a complete snapshot and finds which columns hold a value.

visibility.label: Value visibility
visibility.help: Who may see captured values in clarifications and the cache. Use user-scoped on any source with row-level security.
visibility.none: None — never enumerate values from metadata
visibility.sourceWide: Source-wide — every user of the source sees the same values
visibility.userScoped: User-scoped — values differ per user (row-level security)

unverified.label: Unverifiable filter values
unverified.help: What happens when no evidence can confirm a value: ask (default) or run the query with the value as written and say it was not verified.
unverified.ask: Ask the user for the exact value
unverified.allow: Run the query with the literal as written (disclosed)

probe.label: Confirm on the source
probe.help: Allow one-row confirmation probes and bounded searches on the customer’s database. Only connectors that stop a statement server-side are probed.

distinct.label: Enumerate small uncaptured domains
distinct.help: Allow SELECT DISTINCT on the source for a column the profile proves small and exactly counted. Off = only confirm/search.

denylist.label: Never probe or show
denylist.help: Comma-separated table.column patterns (* wildcards) that are never probed, enumerated or offered, in addition to sensitive-tagged and hidden columns.

existAge.label: Metadata age to prove a value exists (hours)
existAge.help: A snapshot older than this cannot correct a typo on its own; a source probe confirms it instead.

absentAge.label: Metadata age to say a value does not exist (hours)
absentAge.help: Stricter: telling the user a value is absent is shown as a fact.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.desc: Connect Jeen Insights to external services so members — and the assistant, on their behalf — can act on their results, e.g. email a summary, using their own credentials. Every action requires the member's own OAuth consent, admin group approval, and an explicit preview → confirm step.
integrations.removeConfirm: Remove {name}? Members will lose their connections.
integrations.masterOff: Turn on the master switch to add connectors and manage group access.
integrations.noConnectors: No connectors yet. Add one from the catalog below.
integrations.allAdded: All available connectors have been added.
integrations.groupRolesHelp: Map an Entra (Azure AD) group's object ID to a capability role. A member's effective role is the highest of their base role, group role, and any local allow exception.
integrations.allowedDomains: Allowed domains, comma-separated (blank = sender's own domain)
integrations.noGroups: No groups — nobody can connect yet.

enable.label: Enable connectors
enable.help: Master switch for the entire per-user connector platform. While off, no connectors, sign-in flows, or actions are available to anyone.

agentTools.label: Allow agent tool-calling
agentTools.help: Let the assistant propose connector actions (e.g. email a result) for a member. Every call still routes through the same preview → confirm gate and requires the member's OAuth consent + group approval. Requires the master switch above.

myConnections.title: My Connections
myConnections.desc: Connect your own accounts so you can act on results — for example, email a summary from your own mailbox. You control each connection and can disconnect at any time.

title.A: Tier A: SQL rolls the data up first; only per-period totals reach the analysis service.

neutralEgress.A: Only aggregated totals are sent to the analysis service; no row-level data leaves the database. The exact count is recomputed when you run.
neutralEgress.B: Entity rows are sent to the analysis service, capped and audited with the column list. The exact count is recomputed when you run.
